clue.text: Vehicle on course

parts.note: the course is a golf course, and the vehicle is the little buggy players ride between holes

explanation.surface: A car or bus somewhere on its route.
explanation.definitionFit: A buggy used on the links is a small electric vehicle that carries players and clubs round the course.

clue.text: Making a purchase?

parts.note: purchase here is not buying but grip or leverage, so making a purchase means prising with a bar

explanation.definitionFit: Purchase also means mechanical advantage, the grip a crowbar gets, so using a bar to prise something is gaining purchase.

clue.text: Not the only one on the beach

definitions.text: Not the only one on the beach

parts.words: Not the only one on the beach
parts.note: plays on the saying that someone is not the only stone of that kind on the beach, meaning plenty of others exist

explanation.surface: Someone at the seaside who finds they are not alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'not the only one on the beach' tells a jilted lover there are plenty of other choices, alluding to the countless smooth stones on a shore.

clue.text: Avaricious newsman outwardly dismal

indicators.note: the word for dismal sits on the outside, wrapping round the newsman

parts.note: grey weather or a grey mood is dismal
ED, short for editor, the newsman in charge of a paper

explanation.surface: A grasping journalist who looks gloomy on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' says the word for dismal goes round the outside; grey suggests dull, cheerless weather or mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone with an excessive desire for wealth and possessions.

clue.text: I left fancy mince-pies, remarkable type

indicators.note: the I is left out and the remaining letters of the festive pastries are rearranged in a fancy way

explanation.surface: Someone who has turned down the decorated Christmas pastries is an unusual character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I left' takes one I from MINCEPIES, and 'fancy' rearranges the remaining eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a fine or odd specimen describes them as a notable individual of their kind, a remarkable sort.

clue.text: Innkeeper has a perennial plant

parts.note: a landlord who receives guests at an inn is their host

explanation.surface: The landlord of a pub owns a hardy flower.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a shade-loving garden plant with broad leaves that comes back every year, a classic perennial.

clue.text: Mole she's removed has no fixed abode

definitions.note: the definition is a noun phrase, a description of a person's situation, standing for the adjective as in 'of no fixed abode'

indicators.note: the letters of the burrowing animal and the woman are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A mole and a woman have been evicted, so now nobody has a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' is the anagram signal, rearranging MOLESHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Of no fixed abode is the police phrase for someone without a settled place to live.

clue.text: Hit second lorry

parts.note: a truck is the US word for a lorry

explanation.surface: A second lorry was involved in a collision.
explanation.definitionFit: Struck is the past tense of strike, which means to hit.

clue.text: A soldier with deserter on mount

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, gives a gunner or soldier
a rat is one who deserts a cause, like rats leaving a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A soldier and a deserter climb a mountain together.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the mountain in Turkey where Noah's Ark is said to have come to rest.

clue.text: Dear Bella scrambled egg before five inside

indicators.note: the egg-and-five pair goes inside the jumbled name
the name Bella is scrambled like eggs into a new order
the egg comes in front of the five in the inserted pair

parts.note: an egg is round, so it stands for the letter O
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Sweet Bella beat an egg before putting five inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' turns BELLA into LABLE, and 'inside' puts OV after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dear to you is easy to love, adorable and endearing.

clue.text: Poor Rex accepted payment from the funds

indicators.note: the jumbled name takes the payment inside itself
poor Rex is in bad shape, so his letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: a cheque is a written order for a payment

explanation.surface: Penniless Rex took a payment out of the public purse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges the name to EXR, and 'accepted' has it take the payment in before its last letter. The Exchequer is the UK treasury.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the British government's treasury, the department holding the national revenue.

clue.text: See adult gillian not half leading nimbly

indicators.note: the adult and the shortened name go in front of the see

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: not half of the name Gillian is kept: only its front part, the first three of its seven letters, survives

parts.note: Ely, a cathedral city, is a bishop's see, its diocese

explanation.surface: A grown-up girl named Gillian was quick on her feet, half the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps only the front of GILLIAN, giving GIL. A see is the seat of a bishop; Ely in Cambridgeshire is a favourite crossword see.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with quickness and light grace is doing it in a nimble, agile way.

clue.text: Ground-squirrel Tom by itself first mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the result is how the words sound

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, and by itself means mere; the mere comes first, giving mere cat

explanation.surface: A tomcat on its own is the first thing anyone mentions about a burrowing animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts MERE before CAT, and 'mentioned' says MERE CAT is heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In South Africa the name was once also given to the Cape ground squirrel, a burrowing desert animal living in colonies.

clue.text: What to do after slimming to reduce expenditure

definitions.meaning: after dieting your trousers are loose, so you pull the strap round your waist in a notch
to cut back on spending in hard times

explanation.surface: Advice for dieters that doubles as advice on household budgets.
explanation.definitionFit: After losing weight you literally pull your waistband in a notch; figuratively the same phrase means to economise and spend less.

clue.text: Struggle to find battleship

definitions.meaning: a contest of strength, or any tussle between two sides
read as a tug, a kind of ship, belonging to war

explanation.surface: Searching hard for a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope-pulling contest is a trial of strength; cryptically a tug of war is a boat built for battle, a warship.

clue.text: Seeing it isn't a type of sugar

parts.note: isn't contains the negative not
icing sugar is the finely powdered kind used for cake toppings

explanation.surface: Seeing that a substance is not a particular sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Noticing something is observing or spotting it, which is what seeing it means here.

clue.text: Say nothing for drinks machine

parts.note: to say something is to express it
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet about the coffee maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of espresso, the strong coffee and the pressurised machine that brews it.

clue.text: I started off after all the others

indicators.note: the letters of the two words go off in a new direction, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they set off only once everyone else had gone.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest arrival, the one who comes after everyone else, is the slowest and least punctual of all.

clue.text: Should after Thursday be considered

indicators.note: the word for should is placed after the abbreviation

parts.note: ought and should both express obligation

explanation.surface: Something that ought to be pondered after Thursday.
explanation.definitionFit: A considered view is one reflected on carefully, a matter given careful reflection.

clue.text: Journey from junction to become less complicated

parts.note: T stands for a junction, as in a T-junction
ravel can mean to untangle or disentangle, making less complicated

explanation.surface: A journey from a road junction that gets simpler as it goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Ravel usually means tangle, but it also has the opposite sense, to untwist.
explanation.definitionFit: To journey is to go from place to place, to make a trip.

clue.text: Loud protest from bowler?

parts.note: a cricket bowler appealing shouts for the batsman to be given out, a shout that literally names a dismissal

explanation.surface: A man in a bowler hat complains noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler throws the ball at the batsman, and shouts an appeal when the batsman may be dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud public protest is a clamour of objection, and the cricket bowler's cry is quite literally a shout of 'out'.

clue.text: After most of month shaking ripe tree

indicators.note: the shaken letters come after the shortened month
most of the month name is kept, losing only its last letter

parts.note: June is a month

indicators.note: shaking the word ripe jumbles its letters

explanation.surface: Late in the month, a tree is shaken for its ripe fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims JUNE to JUN, and 'shaking' rearranges RIPE into IPER.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen conifer whose berries flavour gin.

clue.text: Beer dispute in the northeast

definitions.note: the definition describes where the place lies rather than naming it as a noun: a town found in that region

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer
a row is a noisy argument

explanation.surface: An argument over a pint in a north-eastern pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Jarrow is a town on the Tyne in north-east England, famous for the 1936 Jarrow March of unemployed workers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyneside town sits in England's north-east region, near Newcastle.

clue.text: One barely recognisable in the colony?

definitions.text: One barely recognisable in the colony?

parts.words: One barely recognisable in the colony?
parts.note: barely here means without clothes, and the colony is a naturist community

explanation.surface: Someone hard to make out among a group of settlers.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist is someone who goes without clothes, and naturist camps are often called colonies.

clue.text: Craftsman in good heart if I certify him!

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words from heart to certify

explanation.surface: A craftsman good at heart, if I vouch for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' tells you to look inside 'heart if I certify'.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a skilled worker or inventor, someone who makes things by hand.

clue.text: Engineer's children have second edition

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps, gives an engineer
issue is a formal word for offspring

explanation.surface: An engineer's children are on their second edition.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprint, a book or record brought out again, is a further edition of it.

clue.text: Early trouble at the seam

indicators.note: trouble disturbs the letters of early, throwing them into a new order

explanation.surface: Early problems at the coal face.
explanation.definitionFit: A seam of coal is a stratum, a band of rock or mineral lying between others.

clue.text: Give up leave

parts.note: leave here is holiday time off work, so giving it up means doing without a break

explanation.definitionFit: To do without something is to give it up or forgo it, as a worker forgoes a holiday.
